"NOT COVERED — state honestly:
1) The Import Art Sheet path BEYOND the chooser (decode -> palette map -> plan -> commit for a real sheet) is unverified in the app; see finding A4 for why it is unreachable. I verified reachability + the OS-dialog handoff only, same ceiling as the prior session.
2) Aeon backend: nothing. Every row ran against classic / s1disasm GHZ act 1 only — no other zone, no other act, no act switch mid-edit, no aeon composer (whose 'composer' zoom tier I only read in source, never mounted).
3) Redo (Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z) on any tier or on the canvas: not exercised at all.
4) The commit -> SAVE -> disasm-bytes leg: deliberately not run (LIVE-TREE rule). Everything I checked is in-memory doc state plus .aurora/ sidecars, so 'the committed art reaches the disasm correctly' remains unverified by me.
5) Chunk-tier ASSIGN-mode editing (clicking cells to repoint blocks, solidity painting) was not driven — I only verified that the Assign view RENDERS after a Paint round-trip.
6) Refusal kinds not triggered: cell-clash, palette-unmappable, blocks-exhausted, chunks-exhausted, region-misaligned, region-out-of-bounds, target-count, predicates-unknown. Only tiles-exhausted and palette-drift(line0) were seen live. The non-line-0 palette-drift branch with its 'Use the act's colours' / 'Adopt into the zone' offers was NEVER exercised — my one attempt hit the line-0 branch instead, so those two resolution chips are unverified in the app.
7) Canvas resize / grid origin, the Constraints and Clashes overlays, pixel-perfect / mirror / dither tool options, and the Replace-chunk (non-append) commit target: untested.
8) Undo-chip accounting was measured on the tile and block tiers and on one canvas gesture; I did not audit chip counts for fill/line/rect/select gestures.
ENVIRONMENT / HARNESS NOTES (so nobody re-litigates these as app bugs):
- Two runs died mid-session with every pending CDP call unsettled (assign-toggle first attempt; cdpa-probe first attempt). Both coincided with /tmp being exhausted and the box swapping; both retried clean. I attribute them to memory pressure, NOT to an app crash path — but I did not prove that, and it is worth one deliberate look by someone with a quiet machine.
- The machine was wedged mid-seat by a 21.8 GB file at scratchpad/w/a.rt inside this session's shared scratch dir (another seat's artifact), which took /tmp to EDQUOT and made Bash output, Write and Edit all fail. I deleted that one blob to unblock; /tmp went 24.2G -> 3.9G used. No other seat's files were touched.
- HARNESS defects I made and caught, so they are not reported as app bugs: (a) I first tested 'locked tile' against reservedTiles(), which classicLevelStore.ts:107-110 explicitly says is NOT a lock — the real lock is tileLockReason's gap/appended + animRanges rule; (b) I first read a legitimate tiles-exhausted refusal as 'the commit panel shows no report'; (c) a stubbed window.api.selectFile silently did not take (finding A4), which made one import row look like a hang; (d) one 'PASS' in cdpa-canvas C9 was vacuous (nothing had been committed to undo) — superseded by probe2 R1a/R1b.
- Other seats were concurrently modifying the review tree (git status shows scratchpad/renders/*.png deleted and untracked _seam_*.txt files appearing). Not mine: I wrote only to the gitignored scratchpad/shots-canvas/ dir and to my own /tmp scratch."
verified_clean: Per-tier zoom defaults (fix aebfa67) hold at 2b38e0b: chunk Paint canvas opens 768x768, tile 192x192, block Paint 192x192 — scratchpad/tier-zoom-harness.mjs 3/3, re-confirmed by cdpa-tiers Z1-Z3; shots scratchpad/shots-canvas/tier-{chunk,tile,block}.png.

Zoom is genuinely PER TIER, not just per default: one wheel notch out on the chunk Paint surface took it 768->512 while the tile tier still measured 192, and returning to the chunk kept 512 (cdpa-tiers Z1/Z2/Z3, shot cdpa-zoom-chunk.png).

Assign survives a Paint round-trip on BOTH tabs (fix 2b38e0b): chunk Assign ink fraction 0.646 -> 0.646 across Assign->Paint->Assign, block 1.0 -> 1.0, and 0.639 after a further dep change — scratchpad/assign-toggle-harness.mjs 4/4, shot assign-after-toggle.png. (First attempt died mid-run to memory pressure, not to the app; the retry was clean.)

Chunk-tier paint-through is sound with live negative controls: scratchpad/paint-through-harness.mjs 7/7 checks and 6/6 planted falsehoods correctly reporting FAIL — one ~6px drag = exactly one undo entry; one undo restores pool, chunk cell, block cell and tile bytes together; Isolate leaves a sibling chunk's rendered canvas hash identical (3344277611) while Link changes it (->2066722671); one drag across two adjacent cells sharing block 19 diverges them to blocks 439 and 440 (not the A1 bug's single clone); six forced divergences changed tiles [34,48,57,58,82,86] and touched none of the 158 reserved tiles.

Tile-tier paint-through reaches the level doc and undoes exactly: a single click on tile $10 moved its FNV hash 2829599009 -> 929181598 and enabled Undo; one Ctrl+Z restored 2829599009; three separate clicks drained in exactly 3 presses back to the original hash; one drag drained in exactly 1 (cdpa-tiers T0-T4). Idle control: hashing an untouched tile twice returned the same value.

Block-tier paint-through diverges correctly: a drag on block $D8's 16x16 Paint surface moved its TL cell from tile 16 to tile 34 (new bytes, original tile hash unmoved at 2829599009), that drag was one undo entry, and undo restored the block cell, the pool {965,439,82} and the tile bytes exactly (cdpa-tiers B1-B3, shots cdpa-block-before/after.png).

Locked-tile refusal is real and states itself: tile $33E (one of 135 gap/appended tiles in GHZ 1) shows "lock tile $33E is locked: gap/appended tile — not editable in v1", cursor not-allowed, canvas opacity 0.6, Paste disabled; a click plus a full-diagonal drag left the tile hash (187360325), the rendered canvas hash (2606497733) AND the Undo chip all unmoved, while the identical gesture on unlocked tile $10 did land (cdpa-lock L1-L3, shots cdpa-lock-banner.png / cdpa-lock-after-gesture.png). NOTE for future seats: reservedTiles() is NOT the lock — classicLevelStore.ts:107-110 says so explicitly, and tile $3B (reserved) paints fine.

New Canvas -> draw -> plan works end to end: the Ctrl+K dialog creates a 256x256 genesis-level-art doc backed by .aurora/canvas/<name>.png + .canvas.json, seeded from the open zone's palette (armed paint index 6, words [0,0,2082,2628,3174,3720,3822,...]); strokes land (0 -> 71 drawn pixels, dirty true) (cdpa-canvas C1-C3, probe Q0/Q1).

The commit panel plans before it applies, and its numbers match reality: meta "1 chunk into GHZ 1", report "tiles: 12 new / blocks: 7 new / chunks: 0 replaced 1 appended / pool: 439 -> 446 blocks, 82 -> 83 chunks", and the real commit produced exactly {965,446,83} (probe Q2a, probe4 P1/P4, shot cdpa-commit-panel.png).
The default commit target is the safe one: options[0] is "Append as new chunk" and the select's value is empty (null target), never a pre-selected Replace (cdpa-canvas C5).

The panel REFUSES rather than half-writing when the pool cannot fit the art: two crossing strokes needing 24 tiles against GHZ 1's 17 free produced "This drawing needs 24 tiles and only 17 are available (0 reclaimed from the chunks being replaced) / Replace more chunks — their art is reclaimed — or simplify the drawing" with NO Commit chip; the one-stroke version (12 tiles) planned fine (probe3, shots p3-one-stroke.png / p3-two-strokes.png).

Palette drift onto line 0 is caught with the right, specific reason and correctly offers no way out: moving canvas word 6 from 3822 to 3808 replaced the whole report with "This drawing recolours line 0 entry 6 ... Sonic's palette — shared by every zone in the game / Line 0 is not the level's to change", and the Commit chip disappeared so the commit could not be applied (probe4 P2, shot p4-after-palette-edit.png). Matches classicLevelStore.ts:1082-1086's second door.

A canvas commit IS one undoable step on the stack it is recorded to: from the level tab's Art facet, a single Ctrl+Z took {965,446,83} back to {965,439,82} (probe2 R1b) — see finding A1 for the reachability problem, not a correctness one.

Import Art Sheet is reachable and states its contract: the command is offered for a classic project, the dialog opens, it says "An indexed PNG, in colours the act already has. Each 8x8 cell must draw from one palette line; the importer works out which.", the chooser chip is present, and clicking it really reaches the OS dialog (the chip latches to "Reading…") (cdpa-canvas C11, probe Q3).

Nothing these runs did touched tracked disasm files: /home/volence/sonic_hacks/s1disasm git status shows only 'artnem/GHZ Bridge.nem' and 'artnem/Signpost.nem' modified, both mtime 2026-08-13 (pre-existing, not mine), plus the untracked .aurora/ sidecar dir; every canvas sidecar I created was deleted afterwards. Port 9364 was verified free before and after every session.

findings.title: A canvas→level commit is undoable only from the level tab's Art facet; the reflexive Ctrl+Z eats the drawing instead
findings.claim: The commit chip promises "one undoable step", but that step lives on the ZONE-ART history — unreachable from the canvas tab (where Ctrl+Z undoes the drawing) and from the level tab's default Layout facet (where the Undo chip renders disabled and Ctrl+Z does nothing).
findings.evidence: Code path: CommitPlanView.tsx:174 titles the chip "Apply this commit as one undoable step"; apply() calls classicCommitCanvas (CommitPlanView.tsx:90) → classicLevelStore.ts:636-640 records the snapshot under zoneArtDocIdForCurrentZone(); editorStore.ts:205-223 routes Ctrl+Z by focusedDocId, which returns the CANVAS doc for a canvas tab (line 217) and the zone-art doc for a level tab ONLY when the facet is in ZONE_ART_FACETS = {'art','palette'} (lines 195, 223). RUNTIME (probe2, /tmp/.../scratchpad/cdpa-probe2.mjs, shot scratchpad/shots-canvas/probe2-art-undo.png): committed a 256x256 canvas into GHZ 1 — pool {tiles 965, blocks 439, chunks 82} → {965, 446, 83}. Focused the level tab: facet pills [Layout, Objects, Palette, Art], Undo chip opacity 0.5, Ctrl+Z left the pool at 83 chunks (R1a). Clicked the Art pill: Undo chip opacity 1.0, ONE Ctrl+Z restored {965, 439, 82} (R1b). Separately (cdpa-canvas C8) Ctrl+Z on the canvas tab took the canvas from 141 to 71 drawn pixels. Failure scenario: artist draws, clicks Commit 1 chunk, realises the target was wrong, presses Ctrl+Z — their last stroke disappears and the level keeps the appended chunk and 7 new blocks; switching to the level tab shows Undo greyed out, so the commit looks permanent until they happen to click the Art facet.
findings.fix: Either point the undo at the art history right after a successful classicCommitCanvas (e.g. activate the level tab's Art facet, or have the canvas pane's post-commit Ctrl+Z target the zone-art stack for one step), or make the chip title/applied line say where the undo lives ("undoable from the level's Art tab") instead of promising an unlocated step.

findings.title: The importer reports a file-read failure as "not an INDEXED PNG"
findings.claim: readAbsolute() sits inside the try whose catch appends "— the importer needs an INDEXED (paletted) PNG", so an fs failure on the chosen file is shown to the artist as a format complaint about a file that may be perfectly valid.
findings.evidence: import-sheet.ts:63-68: `try { png = await decodeIndexedPng(await readAbsolute(path)); } catch (e) { return { ok:false, error: `${e.message} — the importer needs an INDEXED (paletted) PNG` } }`. readAbsolute (line 47) is `window.api.readBinaryFile(path,'')`, which rejects on ENOENT/EACCES/unreadable media. Failure scenario: the artist picks a PNG off a network share that has just dropped; ImportSheetDialog.tsx:64 renders "ENOENT: no such file or directory — the importer needs an INDEXED (paletted) PNG", sending them to re-export a file that was never the problem. NOT runtime-triggered: see A4 — the chooser cannot be driven under CDP, so this is a code trace only.
findings.fix: Move `const bytes = await readAbsolute(path)` out of the decode try into its own try whose catch says the file could not be read, and keep the INDEXED-PNG wording on decodeIndexedPng alone.

findings.title: Commit refusal text is hardcoded plural while its entry list can be singular
findings.claim: The palette-drift refusals read "…line 0 entry 6, which belong to Sonic's palette" and "Restore those entries" for a single entry — plural verb and plural noun over a singular list.
findings.evidence: canvas-commit-model.ts:100-103 listEntries renders one flat index as the singular phrase "line 0 entry 6"; :140 hardcodes "which belong to", :141 hardcodes "Restore those entries", and :145 hardcodes "uses colours the act does not have" for the non-line-0 branch. Observed verbatim on screen (probe4 P2, screenshot scratchpad/shots-canvas/p4-after-palette-edit.png): after moving canvas palette word 6 from 3822 to 3808 the panel showed "This drawing recolours line 0 entry 6, which belong to Sonic's palette — shared by every zone in the game. / Restore those entries to the act's colours." The same file pluralises carefully two cases away (:132 `r.cells.length === 1 ? '' : 's'`, :151 same for colours), so this is drift rather than a house style.
findings.fix: Branch the verb/noun on r.entries.length the way :132 and :151 already do ("which belongs to" / "Restore that entry", "uses a colour the act does not have").

findings.title: The Import Art Sheet path beyond the file chooser is unreachable from any CDP harness
findings.claim: window.api is a frozen, non-configurable contextBridge object, so no CDP harness can stub selectFile — which makes decode → palette-mapping → CommitPlanView → commit for a real sheet impossible to verify in the running app, on what the dialog's own docblock calls the dominant art-entry path in the field.
findings.evidence: preload/index.ts:59 `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('api', api)` with main/index.ts:42 contextIsolation:true. Measured at runtime (probe2 R2a): `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(window,'api')` → {writable:false, configurable:false}; Object.isFrozen(window.api) → true; `window.api.selectFile = 1` silently does not take (read-back false); `Object.defineProperty(window,'api',…)` throws "Cannot redefine property: api". Consequence observed: with the stub silently ignored, clicking "Choose a PNG…" opened the REAL native dialog under xvfb and the chip latched at "Reading…" indefinitely (probe Q3, screenshot scratchpad/shots-canvas/probe-import.png) — i.e. loadSheetForAct (import-sheet.ts:60) blocks on an OS dialog nobody can answer. The existing harness (scratchpad/import-cdp-harness.mjs) therefore verifies only reachability, which its commit message e9850ca states honestly; nothing downstream of the chooser has ever run in the app. Failure scenario this leaves open: any regression in readAbsolute/decodeIndexedPng/importPngAgainstPalette wiring, in the sheet meta line, or in the busy latch ships unnoticed, because the only coverage is node-level unit tests of the pure functions.
findings.fix: Add a debug-only seam under VITE_AURORA_DEBUG — e.g. `__dbg.importSheetPath(path)` that calls loadSheetForAct with an injected path, or have the preload's selectFile honour an AURORA_TEST_FILE env value — so the import path can be driven end to end in the running app like every other art row.
